title: Cluster 04 GAP DRILL: all of Book 2
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 2 · 9 questions · 150 marks · built from the Cluster 1, Cluster 2 and Cluster 3 transcripts, plus three Book 1 gaps that two exposures failed to close
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b); that is the point of the layout.

New this drill: rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A correct guess is not mastery, and the transcript needs to record which is which, because a right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE while a right answer said confidently moves on.

Nine questions, and nine is the number the gap list produced. Fifty-six numbered gaps came out of the three Book 2 sittings, plus eight set pieces you produced correctly and will lose, plus three Book 1 gaps that a whole gap drill failed to close. Grouped by the concept that has to surface, they make nine questions. Nothing here is padding, and nothing was cut to hit a round number.

Three gaps come back from a completely new direction, because the straight version has already failed twice. The amphipathic solvent is described only by its structure and never named, in Q6(c). The active-site residue gap is inverted in Q5(a): two mutants of one enzyme behave differently and you place each substitution. The interchain covalent cross-link gap is set against a single polypeptide that has none, in Q7(b).

Q9 is the question you refused. You said bioethics is not tested. It is: learning outcome 2(m), discuss the bioethics of genetic maternal screening for mutations, including trisomy-21. The command word is discuss, so it needs named stakeholders, both sides and a judgement. This is the only place in the whole syllabus that outcome lives.

Eight set pieces you got right are re-tested anyway. The four structural aberrations (Q3), the PCR advantages and limitations (Q2), the three functions of the 5' cap and the three of the poly(A) tail (Q7), the five levels of control (Q4), the three-level packing ladder (Q8), the four outcomes of a base substitution (Q6), and the covalent bond chain from gene to folded protein (Q7b). A fixed list decays faster than a causal chain, because a chain can be rebuilt under pressure and a list cannot. Producing one correctly once is not evidence it survives to November.

The three Book 1 gaps that have now survived two exposures each. R1, an amphipathic solvent disrupting hydrophobic interactions, where you reached for ionic bonds both times, is now Q6(c) with the solvent given only as a structure. R2, the mark-bearing link that the changed amino acid is part of the active site, is now Q5(a) inverted. R3, collagen's strength coming from covalent cross-links between tropocollagen molecules rather than from peptide bonds inside a chain, is now Q7(b) against a chain that has no cross-links.

Six real images sit in this drill, every one extracted from the paper or chapter it came from and none of them a redrawing: the microsatellite marker and the gel in Q1, the three PCR cycles in Q2, the genetic code in Q6, the poly(A) data in Q7 and the screening table in Q9. Two questions are multiple choice, Q2(a) and Q8(a), and both are real prelim questions with real option-by-option keys; in each you have to say whether every option is right or wrong and why, not find the odd one out.

One warning about scope, since you asked twice. Telomerase, operons, recombinant DNA, cloning, vectors, plasmids, ligation, restriction mapping, RFLP, gene therapy, DNA profiling, Northern blotting and FISH all return zero hits in 9477 and none of them appears here. Malaria and heterozygote advantage belong to Book 7, Biological Evolution, not to Core Idea 2. What survives is the end replication problem, telomere and centromere structure and function, and restriction digestion only as step one of a Southern blot.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicates. Q1 the principle and the ceiling of gel electrophoresis · Q2 PCR advantages, limitations and yield · Q3 structural chromosomal aberrations · Q4 the five levels of gene expression control · Q5 aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase specificity and translational fidelity · Q6 the outcomes of a base substitution and the molecular basis of sickle cell anaemia · Q7 mRNA processing and transcript stability · Q8 DNA packing and chromosome ends · Q9 numerical aberration and the bioethics of maternal screening. No concept is the primary target of two questions, and no question repeats a stem from Cluster 1, 2 or 3.
